_owner: Quinn — canonical narrative spine. App copies this into allbyte-web/src/data/story-spine.json; both the walkthrough render and the save-tree outline read it. Quinn owns names/order/membership; App owns the render. Arc stamps `chapter`+`section` keys onto save_tree_manifest.json nodes (no labels, no structure block — they come from here).
_rules: CHAPTERS are evocative PLACE names in journey order.
'Overworld' is a MODE/view, never a chapter or section label (owner ruling).
SECTIONS are the player-facing gameplay beats. The section name IS the beat name.
difficulty is a per-node FILTER on the save tree, never a grouping level.

Walkthrough scenes group by where the content sits in read-order. Save-tree nodes group by WHICH BEAT THE NODE DROPS YOU INTO (a 'before dungeon' node standing in the Mayor's House belongs to Into the Waterways). See NOTE-1 in QA_CLAUDE_SPINE_UNIFICATION.md.

STEPS are the third level: evocative story/action headers ('Waking Up', 'Finding Aremis' Windmill'), NEVER scene names (owner 2026-07-23). One step may span several scenes — the scenes render under it in order, each with its own directions to the next. Per-scene `title` is the LOCATION only, rendered as a de-emphasized label, not as the heading.

Callout `TO PROGRESS:` marks a story gate whose trigger is unintuitive — the one action that advances the plot when a player would otherwise wander looking for it (e.g. sleeping in Elias' bed). Use it sparingly; it is a gate marker, not a hint.
